rationale: C09 is the immediately preceding World Trade Week proclamation and supplies both the child's operative language almost verbatim and substantial portions of its policy narrative. The two directives share the distinctive formulation that free, fair, and reciprocal trade is essential; focus on farmers, ranchers, manufacturers, entrepreneurs, and a level playing field; describe modernizing trade agreements; and discuss KORUS and replacing the outdated and unbalanced NAFTA with USMCA. C11 is another close predecessor with the same observance formula and trade-policy framing, while C17 shares updated 2020 descriptions of USMCA and the China agreement but is less structurally aligned.

shared_material.child_excerpt: During World Trade Week, we reaffirm that free, fair, and reciprocal trade is essential to driving economic growth
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Free, fair, and reciprocal trade is essential to American and global prosperity. During World Trade Week, we reaffirm our unwavering commitment
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive opening policy formulation and commemorative framing recur with minor revision.

shared_material.child_excerpt: modernize and improve existing trade agreements and to secure new deals that are fair and reciprocal
shared_material.parent_excerpt: working to modernize and improve our agreements, negotiating new trade deals that protect our national security and are based on fairness and reciprocity
shared_material.explanation: The child closely adapts C09's description of the Administration's negotiating program.

shared_material.child_excerpt: end the outdated and unbalanced North American Free Trade Agreement
shared_material.parent_excerpt: renegotiate the outdated and unbalanced North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA)
shared_material.explanation: The same distinctive characterization of NAFTA appears in parallel discussions of USMCA, updated to reflect enactment.

shared_material.child_excerpt: do hereby proclaim May 17 through May 23, 2020, as World Trade Week. I encourage Americans to observe this week with events, trade shows, and educational programs that celebrate the benefits of global trade to our country.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: do hereby proclaim May 19 through May 25, 2019, as World Trade Week. I encourage Americans to observe this week with events, trade shows, and educational programs that celebrate the benefits of trade to our country.
shared_material.explanation: The operative provision is reproduced nearly verbatim, changing only the dates and adding “global.”
